headline: Approved beer garden permit for El Potro, conditional wedding alcohol license for Sevmar, new manager for Olive Garden, and new liquor license for KPOT Korean BBQ.
summary: The Licensing Board approved a one-day alcohol license for a beer garden at El Potro Mexican Grill, 90 Pleasant Valley Street, for July 11th fireworks festivities. It granted a conditional one-day alcohol license to Sevmar Mediterranean Bistro for a July 18th wedding reception at St. Basils, pending updated insurance proof, approved a change of manager at Olive Garden Restaurant, 90 Pleasant Valley Street, and approved a new All-Alcohol and Common Victualler License for KPOT Korean BBQ and Hotpot at 90 Pleasant Valley Street.
decisions: Approved the one-day alcohol license for Mariachi Foods Inc., d/b/a El Potro Mexican Grill, for a beer garden at 90 Pleasant Valley Street on July 11th.

Conditionally approved the one-day alcohol license for Sev Mar LLC, d/b/a Sevmar Mediterranean Bistro, for a July 18th wedding reception at St. Basils, 30 East Street, pending an updated Certificate of Liability Insurance.
Approved the change of manager to Brenden Brandes for GMRI, Inc. d/b/a Olive Garden Restaurant, 90 Pleasant Valley Street.
Approved the new All-Alcohol License and Common Victualler Licenses for KHP Valley Methuen, LLC d/b/a KPOT Korean BBQ and Hotpot, 90 Pleasant Valley Street.

Chairman Chase seconded. Motion approved.

MEETING MINUTES 
 
METHUEN LICENSING BOARD 
SEARLES BUILDING, 41 PLEASANT STREET 
SECOND FLOOR CONFERENCE ROOM #208  
 
Pledge of Allegiance. 
 
Meeting of the Methuen Licensing Board on July 8, 2026, 41 Pleasant Street called to order by Chairman 
Chase. Members present were Chairman Chase and Commissioner Camargo. Commissioners Fisher and 
Melendez were absent. 
 
Approval of the agenda for July 8, 2026. Commissioner Camargo motioned to approve the agenda for July 8, 
2026. Chairman Chase seconded. All in favor. 
  
Approval of minutes from June 11, 2026, licensing meeting. Commissioner Camargo motioned to approve the 
minutes from June 11, 2026, licensing meeting. Chairman Chase seconded. All in favor.  
 
NEW BUSINESS 
 
An application was submitted for a One-Day Alcohol license for Saturday, July 11th, from Mariachi 
Foods Inc., d/b/a El Potro Mexican Grill for a Beer Garden in the parking lot adjacent to their 
establishment at 90 Pleasant Valley Street as part of the 4th of July Fireworks Celebration. 
 
Steve Angelo stepped forward, Superintendent of Parks and Recreation for the city living at 20 
Washington Street, Methuen. Joseph Carreiro also stepped forward as the Business Manager for 
Mariachi Foods Inc., living at 57 Lawrence Rd, Salem, NH. Mr. Carreiro stated they were asked by their 
landlords, the Loop, if they would be willing to have a beer garden in front of their location, El Potro 
Mexican Grill. Mr. Carreiro stated that he would be more than happy to participate in the Methuen 
fireworks celebration for this year (their first time participating). The intention is to have a confined 
space where patrons would be able to consume beverages with two managers on duty, himself included.  
One will be outside, one would be inside, managing crowd control and making sure no one is leaving the 
designated area.  They would have a “dry bar” outside where people take orders. He and his staff would
The City of Methuen is an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer in its Programs and Activities  
be monitoring the area to keep everything under control.  The beer garden would be open from 12pm 
until the end of the festivities.  Steve Angelo stated that the City will be providing metal partitions for 
the beer garden. He stated that in front of El Potro is where the command center for the event will be 
located and that will be where most of the police and medical presence would be.  
 
Chairman Chase asked about the exact entrance to the beer garden area. Mr. Angelo stated that access 
would come from Raising Cane’s parking lot. Chairman Chase then asked if the restricted area marked 
on the “plot plan” with a thick bold line was the area where the barricades would be. Mr. Angelo stated 
no, that this is the area restricted from vehicular traffic and no cars would park there. It’s set up for 
people to put their chairs to watch the festivities and also where the stage will be. Chairman Chase then 
asked exactly where is the restricted area where alcohol is being served? Mr. Angelo stated it is area #3 
on the plot plan, right in front of El Potro.  Chairman Chase asked how many points of access are in that 
restricted area. Mr. Angelo pointed to a sidewalk, and a driveway as areas of access. Chairman Chase 
asked what kind of fencing was being used in the restricted drinking area and Mr. Angelo stated it would 
be metal blockades. Chairman Chase asked if IDs would be checked as people enter the restricted area.  
Mr. Carreiro said yes, they would be checked at the dry bar. Chairman Chase clarified that IDs would be 
checked at point of purchase and not just for entering the area and this was confirmed. Commissioner 
Camargo was asking about the TIPS certification.  
 
Chairman Chase asked if everyone working in the restricted area has TIPS or SERV Safe certification.  
Mr. Carreiro stated that he doesn’t serve alcohol but has SERV Safe certification as manager.  He said 
his colleague Jason is SERV Safe certified.  Chairman Chase asked if everyone working in the restricted 
area is SERV Safe certified. Mr. Carreiro stated not everyone: their servers typically do not have SERV 
Safe certification, only the managers.  Commissioner Camargo asked if the two people monitoring the 
restricted area would be serving as well. Mr. Carreiro stated that he will not be serving but will be 
standing next to the dry bar to be sure everyone is being cooperative and to monitor that all the alcohol 
is being consumed within the restricted area. He will have a walkie talkie to communicate with the 
interior of the restaurant.  
 
Chairman Chase asked why all of their servers are not SERV Safe certified. Mr. Carreiro stated that this 
is not required by law in Massachusetts that every server be SERV Safe trained. Chairman Chase stated 
that he wants to look into this. Mr. Carreiro states that their bar tenders are all TIPS certified but their 
waitstaff is not. Chairman Chase stated that his concern is that people interacting with patrons at the 
tables need that training for making assessments - identifying when a patron is overserved, evaluating 
identification etc. Mr. Carreiro stated that they train all their staff as part of their onboarding and that 
they all carry iPads that have ABCC/Massachusetts information showing what’s a legal ID and what is 
not etc. Chairman Chase asked the Licensing Clerk to get confirmation from the City Solicitor regarding 
any state requirement for TIPS Certification. 
 
Commissioner Camargo made a motion to approve the application submitted for a One-Day Alcohol 
license for Saturday, July 11th, from Mariachi Foods Inc., d/b/a El Potro Mexican Grill for a Beer 
Garden in the parking lot adjacent to their establishment at 90 Pleasant Valley Street as part of the 4th of 
July Fireworks Celebration. Chairman Chase seconded. Motion approved.  
 
 
An application was submitted for a One-Day Alcohol license for Saturday, July 18th from Sev Mar LLC, 
d/b/a Sevmar Mediterranean Bistro, of Salem, NH for a wedding reception to be held at St. Basils, 30 
East Street.
The City of Methuen is an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer in its Programs and Activities  
Laura Hajjar, 33 Mohawk Lane, Brentwood, NH, mom of the groom, came forward. Ashley Green came 
forward as General Manager of SevMar. Chairman Chase confirmed that SevMar is catering an event at 
St. Basils and asked what the hours of the event would be. Ms. Hajjar stated that cocktail hour would be 
at 4:15pm and everything would be over at 9:00pm. Chairman Chase asked what would be done to 
control the flow of alcohol.  Ms. Green stated she and her bar manager would be attending/working at 
the bar and 4 other employees that are servers would be coming. Chairman Chase asked if all the servers 
have TIPS certification and Ms. Green stated that all have TIPS certification. Chairman Chase asked if 
everything was taking place inside and Ms. Green stated that yes, it’s an all-inside event.  Commissioner 
Camargo questioned and expired Liability Insurance Certificate presented, and Ms. Green stated she 
would get the updated certificate from SevMar. The current presented Liability Certificate is dated 
1/11/2023 – 1/11/2024. Chairman Chase said he would consider conditional approval based on getting a 
current Certificate of Liability Insurance to the Licensing Clerk. Ms. Green assured the Board she would 
get it to us.   
 
Commissioner Camargo made a motion for a conditional approval (awaiting a current Certificate of 
Liability Insurance) for the application submitted for a One-Day Alcohol license for Saturday, July 18th 
from Sev Mar LLC, d/b/a Sevmar Mediterranean Bistro, of Salem, NH for a wedding reception to be 
held at St. Basils, 30 East Street. Chairman Chase seconded the motion, no other discussion. All in 
favor. Motion passed pending getting the updated Certificate of Liability Insurance to the Licensing 
Clerk. 
 
 
An application was submitted for a Change of Manager for GMRI, Inc. d/b/a Olive Garden Restaurant, 
90 Pleasant Valley Street. 
 
Brenden Brandes came forward, proposed Manager, living at 386 Rimmon Street, Apt. 3, Manchester, 
New Hampshire. He has been with the company for 11 years and has worked at 6 Olive Gardens. He is 
SERV Safe certified and will get that certification into the Licensing Clerk. There were no questions and 
all paperwork was in order. 
 
Commissioner Camargo made a motion to approve the application submitted for a Change of Manager 
for GMRI, Inc. d/b/a Olive Garden Restaurant, 90 Pleasant Valley Street to be Brenden Brandes. 
Chairman Chase seconded, no other discussion. All in favor, motion passed.  Brenden will email his 
SERV Safe certification to the Licensing Clerk. 
 
 
An application was submitted by KHP Valley Methuen, LLC d/b/a KPOT Korean BBQ and Hotpot at 90 
Pleasant Valley Street for a new All-Alcohol License and Common Victualler Licenses.  
 
Atty Russell Chin came forward, his practice is located at 400 Hancock Street, Quincy, MA. He was 
joined by Rufang Hu (owner) and Lingyan Jiang (liquor license manager). Atty Chin stated they are here 
for an All-Alcohol and Common Victualler license (CVIC has already been approved and granted by 
Inspections/Zoning and all other sign offs). Ms. Hu stated they have been open for 2 weeks and it’s 
going well. Atty Chin stated that owner Rufang Hu has extensive experience in operating a restaurant 
and the liquor license manager, Lingyan Jiang, has certifications, is a United States citizen and is 
familiar with all the laws. Commissioner Camargo asked about service/seating capacity and Atty Chin 
stated that the restaurant’s seating capacity is 190.
The City of Methuen is an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer in its Programs and Activities  
Commissioner Camargo made a motion to accept the application submitted by KHP Valley Methuen, LLC d/b/a 
KPOT Korean BBQ and Hotpot at 90 Pleasant Valley Street for a new All-Alcohol License and Common 
Victualler Licenses. Chairman Chase seconded. No further discussion. All in favor.  
 
No other new business. Commissioner Camargo made a motion to adjourn. Chairman Chase seconded. All in 
favor. Meeting adjourned. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Next meeting will be August 12, 2026. 
 
Respectfully Submitted by 
Beth Rizzo 
Licensing Clerk
